messages:
maria: quick heads up — i'm OOO saturday morning 06:00-10:30 PT. leaving devon as primary and sam as secondary for that window.

maria: devon — i left a short checklist in the runbook, critical bits: routing policy, fallback model ids, and contact matrix. link: https://console.internal/runbooks/oncall-handoff

devon: got it, thanks. i'll be primary for the window. sam — can you be ready to take over if i need to step out?

sam: yes i can. i'll be available and have pager enabled. pls set escalation thresholds in the note so i don't second-guess.

maria: escalation thresholds i used: :rotating_light:
- SEV2 (customer visible but partial degradation): sustained error rate > 8% for 10m OR p95 latency > 2s for 5m -> page primary + secondary.
- SEV1 (service down or major outage): any 5xx spike > 25% or sustained queue depth > 500 -> page primary + SRE lead + oncall manager.
- Security/compromise -> immediate page to sec-oncall and engineering director.

devon: adding practical notes — if page shows "model-serving: high-latency" start with these checks:
```
1) `redwood-ctl status model-pool`
2) check GPU saturation: `nvidia-smi -l 1` (or metrics in Console)
3) tail logs on the serving node: `kubectl -n inference logs -f deploy/serving-runtime`
```

anya: also watch the cache hit metrics. sometimes a cold cache causes p95 spikes even when pods are fine. cache-hit < 60% + latency up -> consider prefix cache warmup.

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: incident-1912 "inference-p95-spike". Severity: potential SEV2. Triggers: p95 2.3s over 7m, error rate 4%. Notified: @devon, @sam.

devon: i'm on it. checking routing and recent deploys.

devon: no recent deploys in last 2 hours. `redwood-ctl routes` shows 3/5 GPUs at 85% utilization and one pod with high OOM kills in logs — looks like one replica restarted a few times.

kevin: tagging infra — if a replica keeps restarting we should check node memory pressure; i can look at node logs and evictions.

sam: i'm watching customer-facing metrics. only a handful of customers show degradation (3 customers, highest impact for a batch job). recommend notify CS with short note and mitigation ETA if we exceed thresholds.

maria: for the handoff note — if you escalate to SRE lead, include: recent deploy ids, GPU utilization, cache-hit ratio, and which model variant is routed. keeps the bridge short.

devon: mitigation plan i'm trying: 1) cordon/replace the flappy node 2) scale up transient replica pool by +2 (if quota allows) 3) enable temporary fallback to quantized variant with `route: quantized-1.2` for non-latency-sensitive customers. will post commands once validated.

oncall-bot: action recorded in incident-1912 timeline by devon.

anya: small operational tip — use the console route override with `max_inflight=1` on heavy customers to prevent long-tail blocking other requests.

devon: patched node, scale +2 started. p95 trending down to 1.4s. keeping monitoring for 15m window.

sam: i'm drafting the customer note: "We're investigating increased model latency affecting a subset of jobs. Mitigation underway; next update in 20 minutes." sending to CS now.

kevin: node logs show oom_killed process at 05:12 — may be a memory leak in that model-variant. i'll open a follow-up ticket for debug.

maria: thanks team. devon/sam — please confirm primary/secondary handoff completion in this thread before you close the window. if the issue recurs after i return, follow escalation matrix above and page SRE lead first before execs.

devon: confirmed — i've completed mitigation steps and monitoring looks stable. i'll remain primary until 11:00 PT for a buffer.

sam: confirmed as secondary and on pager.

sre-lead: noted. if anything changes, page me directly (pager key). i'll triage if we see error rate > 12% or p95 > 2.5s sustained.

maria: perfect. leaving the thread. :white_check_mark:
